name: Bile Acid CoA Ligase Deficiency and Defective Amidation

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal bile acid profile with accumulation of atypical bile acid intermediates in plasma and urine
Identification of pathogenic variants in the SLC27A5 gene encoding bile acid CoA ligase
Clinical presentation including neonatal cholestasis and liver dysfunction
Histological evidence of cholestatic liver disease with giant cell transformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal bile acid profile plus pathogenic SLC27A5 variants with compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by biochemical and genetic testing; liver biopsy is supportive but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent jaundice in the neonatal period
searchTerms: newborn jaundice with bile flow blockage
early liver bile buildup in baby

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated atypical bile acid intermediates in plasma and urine
searchTerms: high unusual bile acids in blood and urine
atypical bile substances in body fluids

common.notes: Enlarged liver on physical exam or imaging
Poor weight gain and growth delay

common.symptomName: Prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
searchTerms: slow blood clotting from vitamin K lack
prolonged bleeding time due to vitamin deficiency
coagulation delay caused by vitamin K shortage
scarring of liver progressing to cirrhosis

occasional.notes: Fat malabsorption due to bile acid deficiency

searchTerms: brain and nerve problems with low muscle tone

rare.symptomName: Osteopenia or rickets due to fat-soluble vitamin deficiency
rare.notes: Vitamin D deficiency related bone disease
searchTerms: bone thinning or soft bones from vitamin deficiency
rickets or osteopenia due to fat-soluble vitamin lack

laboratory: Abnormal bile acid profile with atypical intermediates
imaging: Signs of liver fibrosis or cirrhosis on elastography or MRI
other: Liver biopsy showing cholestasis with giant cell transformation

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of abnormal bile acid intermediates characteristic of CoA ligase deficiency

differentialDiagnoses.diseaseId: bile acid synthesis defects type 1 (3β-hydroxy-Δ5-C27-steroid oxidoreductase deficiency)
distinguishingFeatures: Distinct bile acid metabolite profile on biochemical testing

redFlags: Persistent neonatal cholestasis with failure to thrive
Coagulopathy unresponsive to vitamin K supplementation
Rapid progression to liver fibrosis or cirrhosis
